solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Happen to store cooked dish for resident

indicators.note: to store something is to keep it inside, so one word's letters hold the other's

parts.note: to happen is to occur
a pie is a baked dish

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep a hot meal waiting for whoever lives in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever lives in or holds a property is its occupier, the person in residence.

clue.text: Remarkable gesture

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means notable or striking, as in a ... achievement
a sign or movement made to convey a message

explanation.surface: A notable movement of the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal works both as a noun, a sign given by movement, and as a rarer adjective meaning conspicuous or outstanding.

clue.text: So my care is to propagate a tree

indicators.note: propagating breeds new stock, so these letters are bred into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A gardener announces that their job is now to raise new trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to propagate' fits the tree surface but is the anagram signal on SO MY CARE.
explanation.definitionFit: The sycamore is a large maple-like broadleaf species common in Britain.

clue.text: Catch small horse

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a nag is an old or poor horse

explanation.surface: A pony is being caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a hidden drawback or problem, the catch in a deal.

clue.text: Shy about fighting heartless duel, being faint-hearted

indicators.note: about means around, so the shy word wraps round the rest

parts.note: coy means shy or bashful
war is fighting

indicators.note: a heartless word has lost its middle letters, here the two central ones

parts.note: a duel is a fight between two people

explanation.surface: Someone who shies away from a duel is mocked as faint-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' tempts as the definition beside 'faint-hearted', but it is wordplay; 'heartless' strips the middle of the duel word and 'about' wraps the shy word round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Being faint-hearted is lacking courage, the core sense of cowardly.

clue.text: Fellow, mature, is to cope

parts.note: a fellow is a man
to mature is to age

explanation.surface: A grown man must learn to cope.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage is to cope or get by in difficult circumstances.

clue.text: In here, a modest quantity of paper

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone is handing over only a small amount of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a modest' quantity misleads: a ream is 500 sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a stationery measure, now 500 sheets of paper.

clue.text: Fighting court case

definitions.meaning: ... means combat, as in killed in ...

explanation.surface: A legal battle described as a fight in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Action means military combat and also a legal proceeding, a lawsuit.

clue.text: A river bird and parent create Nile blockage

parts.note: a swan is a bird usually seen on rivers
a dam is a mother, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: A swan and its mother somehow block the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: DAM is the parent and also the kind of blockage the whole answer is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aswan Dam in Egypt holds back the waters of the Nile.

clue.text: Make a face, finally smashing vase

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word smashing

parts.note: an urn is a kind of vase

explanation.surface: Someone grimaces after at last breaking a vase.
explanation.definitionFit: To gurn is to pull a grotesque face, a British word known from gurning contests at country fairs.

clue.text: Start to relish a good scrap

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here of relish

explanation.surface: Someone begins to enjoy a proper fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' suggests a fight; here it is a scrap of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag is a scrap of old cloth.

clue.text: Had a blow-out, account unpaid

parts.note: a bill is an account of money due
money unpaid is still owed

explanation.surface: Someone splurged on a big meal and left the bill unpaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow-out' suggests a lavish meal; here it is a sail or cloud swelling outward.
explanation.definitionFit: Sails or smoke that billowed swelled and bulged outward, as if blown out by the wind.

clue.text: All I have to do is to sort out dark wool

indicators.note: sorting out puts things into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A knitter complains that their only task is untangling dark yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: Your workload is the total of tasks you have to get through.

clue.text: So in Rome I can embrace Romeo

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one word's letters hold the other

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, the self
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A lover in Rome hopes to hug Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rome' and 'Romeo' sit side by side, but only Romeo gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, the Roman word for so.

clue.text: Canada youngsters try gin cocktails perhaps

parts.note: to have a go is to try
a gin sling is a cocktail, so slings are drinks of that kind, signalled by perhaps

explanation.surface: Young Canadians are urged to sample gin drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canada youngsters' are not Canadian teens but young Canada geese.
explanation.definitionFit: Goslings are young geese, and the Canada goose is a familiar species.

clue.text: Out of hospital, damages limbs

indicators.note: out of signals that the hospital letter leaves the word

parts.note: harms means damages
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A patient discharged from hospital injures their arms and legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms are the upper limbs of the body.

clue.text: Cane joker in school

indicators.note: in places the joker's letters inside the school abbreviation

parts.note: a wit is a joker or clever humorist

explanation.surface: A prankster at school gets caned.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch is a thin flexible rod used for beating, much like a cane.

clue.text: Cavalier is solitary, abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so these letters run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A lone dashing gentleman left to his fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cavalier' reads as carefree; it is a supporter of King Charles I in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cavaliers were the king's side in the English Civil War, so a Cavalier is a royalist.

clue.text: Held in both hands, carefully move account book

indicators.note: held in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right, the two hands
to edge is to move slowly and carefully

explanation.surface: Someone inches forward clutching a heavy accounts volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledger is the bookkeeping volume where accounts are recorded.

clue.text: Wife getting fine frying pan

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife, as in genealogies
OK means fine

explanation.surface: A wife is given a good pan for frying.
explanation.definitionFit: A wok is a round-bottomed Chinese pan used for stir-frying.

clue.text: VAT on a musical instrument

parts.note: a vat is a large tub; the capitals tempt you to read value added tax

explanation.surface: Sales tax charged on an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'VAT' looks like value added tax but is the vessel, a tub.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is the large, low-pitched brass instrument.

clue.text: Show appreciation of cold drink

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
to lap is to drink with the tongue, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Someone praises a chilled drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapping your hands is how an audience shows it enjoyed something.

clue.text: Platform One: miserable having to go back across it

indicators.note: across it says the reversed word spans the letter for one
going back means reading the word for miserable from right to left

parts.note: sad means miserable
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone on Platform One is fed up at having to return across the station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go back' turns SAD into DAS, and 'across it' puts that around I. 'Platform One' reads as a railway platform.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform at one end of a hall for speakers.

clue.text: Sprinkle black bird in parched area

parts.note: to dust is to sprinkle with a powder
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: Someone scatters something over a dark bird in a dry region.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust bowl is a drought-stricken region whose topsoil blows away, like 1930s America.

clue.text: Retaliate for some craven gentleman

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone takes revenge on behalf of a cowardly man.
explanation.definitionFit: To avenge a wrong is to retaliate for it by punishing the wrongdoer.

clue.text: Worked in kitchen, lacking any energy

definitions.meaning: to wash up is to clean dishes after a meal

explanation.surface: A kitchen worker is worn out by the dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Washed up is the past of doing the dishes and also an idiom for being spent or past it.
